title: Buy Now Pay Later is QUIETLY Burying Americans in Debt... | BNPL Crisis
summary: A faith-based finance channel reacts to BNPL horror stories: rent financing, credit bureau reporting, and stacking debt across apps.

assertions.quote: Affirm just partnered with a company called Assusu, which helps people finance their monthly rent with buy now pay later
lenders see it as an unhealthy spending habit because they see it as you not being able to manage your cash

verdicts.note: Manual mortgage underwriters do flag BNPL activity on bank statements as a cash-flow concern, but it isn't an automated score factor and its weight varies by lender.

assertions.quote: Klarna and Affirm are now reporting to credit bureaus
You are robbing Peter to pay Paul and all types of different financial gymnastics
If I'm in an online checkout and I can't afford to buy something right then and there, then I can't afford to buy it

verdicts.note: This is a personal affordability rule framed as a value judgment rather than a claim that can be checked against evidence.

assertions.quote: they find a way to pay for the things that they actually don't need by going into debt

verdicts.note: Anecdotes and some survey data support this pattern among heavy BNPL users, but it isn't a rigorously measured, universal behavior.

assertions.quote: If you would just save the money, you'd be paying the lowest possible price for the things that you want
because I keep paying off all of my purchases before they are due, they're just not giving me money no more

verdicts.note: A plausible underwriting incentive, but this is based on a single customer's anecdote and phone call, not documented lender policy.
